subject: Price buckets — anchoring, smoothing, and minimums (order form redline review)
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Acero — order form and pricing bucket questions

Team — forwarding Acero's redline (attached). They're asking us to: 1) tighten the definition of the "price bucket anchoring" in Exhibit B so it doesn't cascade into a full true-up when usage drops one slab; 2) add an explicit smoothing credit for quarterly volatility; and 3) cap the downside floor for the first 12 months at 65% of committed value.

Quick asks: 1) Laura — are these acceptable legal positions or do we push back on the 65% hard floor? 2) Rishi — if we accept smoothing credits, what's the P&L impact for Q4 / next 12 months (ballpark)? 3) Karthik — I want a single-paragraph response to the customer that offers a path forward (compromise language).

Attachments: ACERO_OrderForm_PricingRedline_v3.docx, redline-pricing-exhibit.pdf

Thanks,
Hannah

Subject: Acero redlines: pricing bucket anchoring and smoothing (attached)

Hannah — thanks for the call earlier. We uploaded our marked-up order form for your review (attached). A couple of clarifying notes inline: 1) our concern with "anchoring" language in Exhibit B is that a single drop in usage could re-trigger a full-band true up that retroactively increases our invoice; we want a "buffer" to avoid month-to-month noise driving financial adjustments; 2) we proposed a quarterly smoothing credit to be applied when month-to-month variance exceeds 30% of the rolling average; 3) we proposed a downside floor of 65% of committed spend for the first 12 months to account for our go-to-market seasonality.

We are willing to split the difference on the smoothing calibration (30% -> 35%) and accept a reserve true-up window of 60 days, if Redwood will accept the 65% floor for the first year.

Subject: RE: Acero redlines: pricing bucket anchoring and smoothing (attached)

Hannah — high level legal take below. I annotated the Word redline as well but calling out the main risks here so Karthik and Rishi can factor in commercial: 

- 65% floor for first 12 months: legal is comfortable with a time-bound floor, provided we explicitly exclude force majeure and agreed project delays (we should add an exceptions list). Also require that the floor only applies to billed committed spend, not to invoice-level usage surcharges.

- Anchoring / buffer: propose we reword to a "deactivation buffer" clause that requires a sustained drop of at least two consecutive monthly slabs (or rolling 45 days) before a true-up applies. This limits snap-backs while preserving our ability to true-up for genuine scale-downs.

- Smoothing credit: we can accept a quarterly smoothing credit, but must define the calculation in Exhibit B (formula with rolling average, variance threshold, and cap on total quarterly credits to 5% of committed spend).

I'll attach my redline. If we accept the 65% floor, add a short repayment / clawback provision if Acero later terminates for convenience within year two. That protects us from immediate revenue loss.

—Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Commercial | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Acero redlines: pricing bucket anchoring and smoothing (attached)

Quick finance read — numbers are estimates but directional: 

- If we accept a 65% downside floor for months 1–12, worst-case recognized revenue impact (if utilization collapses to 0) is ~35% of committed ARR for that year. For the ACERO-1859 package that equates to ~$520k incremental risk in year 1.

- Quarterly smoothing credit capped at 5% of committed spend: on the ACERO numbers that would reduce revenue recognition by up to ~$74k per quarter in high-variance scenarios.

- Recommendation: accept time-bound 65% floor if we get 1) a 60-day true-up notice window, 2) an early-termination clawback that recoups 50% of the floor benefit if they terminate within 12 months, and 3) a clear cap on cumulative smoothing credits (5%).

If legal is comfortable with the clawback and buffer wording, finance can sign off.

—Rishi
VP, Finance | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Tomas Rivera <tomas.rivera@acerohealth.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acero redlines: pricing bucket anchoring and smoothing (attached)

Julia — thanks for the clear redline and for proposing practical options. We reviewed your requests internally and wanted to propose a compromise that we think balances Acero's seasonality with Redwood's need for predictable economics. Proposed summary (we've attached a clean markup for quick review):

1) Buffer before true-up: we will adopt a deactivation buffer that requires two consecutive monthly slab drops (or 45 continuous days) before a true-up triggers. This prevents single month noise from cascading into full true-ups.

2) Time-bound downside floor: we will accept a 65% downside floor for months 1–12 on committed billed spend, with the following conditions: a) exceptions for force majeure and documented project delays; b) a 60-day true-up window; and c) if Redwood grants the floor and Acero terminates for convenience within 12 months, Redwood reserves the right to recover 50% of the floor benefit via a pro rata clawback on the final invoice.

3) Smoothing credit: we will implement a quarterly smoothing mechanism where variance > 35% of the rolling monthly average triggers a smoothing credit. Credits will be calculated per Exhibit B (rolling average formula) and capped at 5% of committed spend per quarter.

If that sounds fair, we can incorporate Laura's precise contractual language and send an updated order form + signature block. Would you prefer a DocuSign for the amended order form or an exchange of executed PDFs?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
